explanations.answer: Them and their children and grandchildren
explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. Moses, Israel's leader, says it's “you and your children and grandchildren” who may fear the LORD all the days of their lives (Deuteronomy 6:2). Three generations in one sentence. Nobody gets left on the bench.

explanations.answer: Only the men of fighting age
explanations.explanation: Not quite, friend. Moses, Israel's leader, never narrows it to fighting men. He says “you and your children and grandchildren” (Deuteronomy 6:2). That means the little ones and the grandkids are in this too.

explanations.answer: Only the heads of each family
explanations.explanation: Close, but Moses, Israel's leader, doesn't hand this to just the head of the house. He puts children and grandchildren right in the sentence with them (Deuteronomy 6:2). The whole family is at this table, baker.

Yep. Moses says to be careful to observe these commands “so that you may prosper and multiply greatly in a land flowing with milk and honey” (Deuteronomy 6:3). He adds that this is just as the LORD, the God of their fathers, has promised. Milk and honey, baker. Sounds like a good place to set up an oven.

This one is true, friend. Moses says to be careful to observe, “so that you may prosper and multiply greatly in a land flowing with milk and honey” (Deuteronomy 6:3). He says it's just as the LORD, the God of their fathers, has promised. Read it again and the whole line is right there.

That's it. “The LORD our God, the LORD is One” (Deuteronomy 6:4). One LORD, baker, and that's the line Moses wants them to hear most. Later in this same sermon he tells them to serve Him only (Deuteronomy 6:13).

Not what Moses says, friend. He says “The LORD our God, the LORD is One” (Deuteronomy 6:4). And a few verses later he calls Him the LORD “who is among you” (Deuteronomy 6:15). Far away just isn't in this sermon.
Nope, and Moses is clear about it. “The LORD our God, the LORD is One” (Deuteronomy 6:4). He's One, baker. Moses also says to serve Him only (Deuteronomy 6:13), so there's no second seat anywhere.
Right, baker. “All your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength” (Deuteronomy 6:5). That's heart, soul and strength, with none held back. I hold on to that one.

Almost, but Moses doesn't leave a piece out. He says to love the LORD your God “with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength” (Deuteronomy 6:5). Most is how I treated the last cookie in the batch, and that's no way to love God. The word is all.

Some is a small word, friend, and Moses doesn't use it here. He says “with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength” (Deuteronomy 6:5). Heart, soul and strength each get the whole word all.
Yes, baker. Moses says “you shall teach them diligently to your children” (Deuteronomy 6:7). And diligently means he's not asking for a once-a-year talk. These words get passed down on purpose.
Good thought, but that's not what the verse says. Moses says “you shall teach them diligently to your children” (Deuteronomy 6:7). The teaching starts at home, friend.
Not this time, baker. Moses tells the people to teach these words diligently “to your children” (Deuteronomy 6:7). The verse doesn't mention priests at all. It sends the teaching right to the kids.

That's a miss, friend, because the Sabbath isn't in this verse. Moses says to speak of these words “when you sit at home and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up” (Deuteronomy 6:7). That covers an ordinary day from morning to bedtime. The answer is false.

Right. Moses never says Sabbath here. He says to speak of them “when you sit at home and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up” (Deuteronomy 6:7). That's every kind of day, baker, from sunrise to bedtime.

You got it. Moses says “Tie them as reminders on your hands and bind them on your foreheads” (Deuteronomy 6:8). That's right where your eyes and hands are all day. Hard to forget something you keep bumping into.
Close, but Moses names different spots. He says “Tie them as reminders on your hands and bind them on your foreheads” (Deuteronomy 6:8). Belts and sandals don't come up in this sermon, friend.

Not those, baker. Moses says “Tie them as reminders on your hands and bind them on your foreheads” (Deuteronomy 6:8). The writing on their houses and gates comes in the next verse, and tents and banners aren't in it.
Yep. Moses says “Write them on the doorposts of your houses and on your gates” (Deuteronomy 6:9). Walk in or walk out, baker, and the words are right there. It's a reminder at every door.
This one is true, friend. Moses says “Write them on the doorposts of your houses and on your gates” (Deuteronomy 6:9). Doorposts and gates are the spots. Every time you go in or out, there it is.

explanations.answer: Wells and vineyards and olive groves
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. Moses says the land has “wells that you did not dig, and with vineyards and olive groves that you did not plant” (Deuteronomy 6:11). Somebody else did all that digging and planting. Israel just walks in.

explanations.answer: Herds of cattle and flocks of sheep
explanations.explanation: Good guess, but that's not on Moses' list. He names “houses full of every good thing,” wells, vineyards and olive groves (Deuteronomy 6:11). Livestock doesn't come up in this part, friend.

Not on this list, baker. Moses says the land has “wells that you did not dig, and with vineyards and olive groves that you did not plant” (Deuteronomy 6:11). There are no chariots in the lineup, just wells and trees ready to go.

That's the warning, baker. “Be careful not to forget the LORD who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery” (Deuteronomy 6:12). Moses says it right after talking about eating and being satisfied. I'd say an oven full of warm cookies can make anybody forget a few things.

Not what Moses says, friend. His warning is “be careful not to forget the LORD who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery” (Deuteronomy 6:12). Harvest waste isn't mentioned in this passage.

Not quite, baker. Moses warns “be careful not to forget the LORD who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery” (Deuteronomy 6:12). Nothing in this passage says to stop working the fields. It's all about remembering the LORD.
Yep. Moses says “Fear the LORD your God, serve Him only, and take your oaths in His name” (Deuteronomy 6:13). Fear, serve and swear, all pointed at Him. That's a full list for one verse, baker.

It's true, friend. Moses says “Fear the LORD your God, serve Him only, and take your oaths in His name” (Deuteronomy 6:13). Three things, and all of them are for the LORD. Check it again and you'll see them lined up.
You got it. Moses says “Do not follow other gods, the gods of the peoples around you” (Deuteronomy 6:14). That's the peoples living around Israel, baker. Their gods are the ones not to follow.
Not this time, friend. Moses says “Do not follow other gods, the gods of the peoples around you” (Deuteronomy 6:14). The Egyptians aren't named in that warning. It's the peoples around them.
Not quite, baker. Moses says “Do not follow other gods, the gods of the peoples around you” (Deuteronomy 6:14). He points to the peoples around them, and kings across the sea don't come up.

That's the word, baker. “Do not test the LORD your God as you tested Him at Massah” (Deuteronomy 6:16). Massah is a place Israel knew, and Moses points back to it. I'd say that's a lesson in not repeating yourself.
Close, but flee isn't the word. Moses says “Do not test the LORD your God as you tested Him at Massah” (Deuteronomy 6:16). It's test, friend.
Not quite, baker. Moses says “Do not test the LORD your God as you tested Him at Massah” (Deuteronomy 6:16). The word he uses is test, not curse.

explanations.answer: It goes well and they possess the land
explanations.explanation: That's it. Moses says to do what is right and good “so that it may be well with you and that you may enter and possess the good land” (Deuteronomy 6:18). The good land the LORD swore to give their fathers. Well and possessed, baker.

explanations.answer: They become the rulers over Egypt
explanations.explanation: Egypt is behind them, friend. Moses says doing what is right and good is “so that it may be well with you and that you may enter and possess the good land” (Deuteronomy 6:18). There's nothing about ruling Egypt anywhere in this passage.

explanations.answer: Their enemies make peace with them
explanations.explanation: Not what Moses says, baker. He says they will “enter and possess the good land,” “driving out all your enemies before you, as the LORD has said” (Deuteronomy 6:18-19). Driving out is the picture, and peace treaties don't appear here.
Yep. Moses says the land comes “driving out all your enemies before you, as the LORD has said” (Deuteronomy 6:19). That's what he says taking the land includes. He's not hiding it, baker.

Moses actually says it, friend. The land comes “driving out all your enemies before you, as the LORD has said” (Deuteronomy 6:19). So taking the land does include driving out all their enemies. The answer is true.

That's the word, baker. “We were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt” (Deuteronomy 6:21). Pharaoh was Egypt's king. The answer to the son starts at the lowest point and then tells how the LORD brought them out.

That would've been a nicer story, friend. But Moses says “We were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt” (Deuteronomy 6:21). Pharaoh was Egypt's king. Guests get a snack, and slaves in Egypt got a very different deal.
Not neighbors, baker. Moses says “We were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt” (Deuteronomy 6:21). Pharaoh was Egypt's king. That's where the answer to the son begins.

You got it. “He brought us out from there to lead us in and give us the land that He had sworn to our fathers” (Deuteronomy 6:23). Out of Egypt and into the land, baker. That's the answer the son hears.
Not quite, friend. The line says “to lead us in and give us the land that He had sworn to our fathers” (Deuteronomy 6:23). The word is land, and kingdom isn't in that verse.
No throne in this verse, baker. It says the LORD brought them out “to lead us in and give us the land that He had sworn to our fathers” (Deuteronomy 6:23). What He swore to give was the land.

Yep. The answer says “the LORD commanded us to observe all these statutes and to fear the LORD our God, that we may always be prosperous and preserved, as we are to this day” (Deuteronomy 6:24). Prosperous and preserved, baker. And it adds as we are to this day.

That one's true, friend. The answer says “the LORD commanded us to observe all these statutes and to fear the LORD our God, that we may always be prosperous and preserved, as we are to this day” (Deuteronomy 6:24). It's right there in the words Moses gives for the son.
